RATE SCHEDULE

General Service Metered Demand (Lassen Municipal Utility District)

FIG. 01 — REFERENCE IMAGE

[ Photo: commercial utility meter ]

The Short Answer: General Service Metered Demand (Lassen Municipal Utility District) is this is the official general service metered demand commercial tariff offered by lassen municipal utility district in dc. On a commercial bill, this line typically indicates reduce kwh exposure.

FIG. 02 — STRUCTURAL CONTEXT

Why Utilities Use This Model

This specific tariff is filed by Lassen Municipal Utility District with the DC public utility commission. It dictates exactly how your facility's energy and demand consumption is priced, and serves as the legal basis for your monthly commercial billing.

🧮 Worked Scenario

If your monthly bill is $1,000 and you used 5,000 kWh, your blended effective rate is 20¢/kWh. If this General Service Metered Demand (Lassen Municipal Utility District) increases by 10%, your total bill rises to $1,100 even if your usage stays exactly the same.

FIG. 03 — COMMON ERRORS

The Common Misread

The most common mistake is assuming owners assume all kwh cost the same, ignoring tiered volume thresholds. In reality, the billing structure separates these mechanics to reflect grid realities.

How to spot this: Check the top right corner of your bill for "Rate Schedule" or "Service Classification." Common codes include "GS-2", "E-19", or "Large TOU".

🎯 Your One Action This Week

Focus on reduce kwh. Review your last two bills to see if this specific lever is driving your costs.
